_what_this_is: Two voices for BRUNSWICK HALT. Materials in this world's language; every horizontal anchor is the tiled dado band's top edge at 1.20 m.

dado_band.line: the tiled dado band's top edge above the floor
dado_band.sentence: A clearly legible dark bottle-green glazed tiled dado band runs corner to corner on every exposed wall surface including the side-wall returns, its top edge at exactly 1.20 m above the floor, interrupted only by the doorway.
dado_band.label: DADO BAND TOP 1.20 M ABOVE FLOOR - GATE ANCHOR
dado_band.why: This station's universal anchor: every wall below ground carries the same glazed dado band with its top edge at one height. A painter draws it and the instrument finds it.

booking_hall_tiled.why: The booking hall is the station's public face: full-height glazed tiling laid once in 1931 and polished ever since.
booking_hall_tiled.walls: cream crackle-glazed rectangular wall tiles above the dado band; below the band, dark bottle-green glazed tiles with a moulded black tile capping
booking_hall_tiled.ceiling: a flat white plaster ceiling with a deep moulded cornice
booking_hall_tiled.floor: buff terrazzo divided by narrow brass strips into large squares
booking_hall_tiled.blank: unbroken cream crackle-glazed tiling above the dado band with dark bottle-green glazed tiles below

platform_vault.why: The platform is the deep room: the same tiling running away down its whole length under a painted soffit, everything slightly sooted.
platform_vault.walls: cream crackle-glazed rectangular wall tiles above the dado band, lightly sooted toward the top; below the band, dark bottle-green glazed tiles; a single blank vitreous-enamel disc mounted on the wall
platform_vault.ceiling: a broad flat-painted concrete soffit springing from a moulded cornice line
platform_vault.floor: smooth grey concrete, a single worn white painted guidance line running down its length
platform_vault.blank: unbroken cream crackle-glazed tiling above the dado band with dark bottle-green glazed tiles below
